import numpy as np

# NASA outlay data in millions for FY 2008-2017
data = [17834, 19168, 18906, 17617, 17190, 16978, 17093, 18272, 18828, 18698]

# Sort the data
sorted_data = sorted(data)
print("Sorted data (in millions):", sorted_data)

# 10% of 10 data points = 1 data point
# Winsorize: replace extremes with next closest values
n = len(data)
k = int(0.10 * n)  # 1 data point
print(f"k (10% of {n}): {k}")

# For 10% Winsorized mean, we replace the lowest k values with the (k+1)th smallest value
# and the highest k values with the (k+1)th largest value

winsorized = sorted_data.copy()
# Replace the lowest k values with the (k)th smallest value (1st replaced by 2nd smallest)
winsorized[0:k] = [sorted_data[k]] * k
# Replace the highest k values with the (k)th largest value
winsorized[-k:] = [sorted_data[-(k+1)]] * k

print(f"Winsorized data: {winsorized}")

# The 10% Winsorized range is the difference between the max and min of the winsorized data
winsorized_min = min(winsorized)
winsorized_max = max(winsorized)

print(f"Winsorized min: {winsorized_min}")
print(f"Winsorized max: {winsorized_max}")

winsorized_range = winsorized_max - winsorized_min
print(f"10% Winsorized range (in millions): {winsorized_range}")

# Convert to billions (divide by 1000)
winsorized_range_billions = winsorized_range / 1000
print(f"10% Winsorized range (in billions): {winsorized_range_billions}")

# Round to hundredths place
print(f"Rounded to hundredths: {round(winsorized_range_billions, 2)}")
EOF
